name: Minor-Admissible Trace Positivity Is Disjunctive and Nonaffine
statement: For the fixed six-component pair $(A,C)$ from the three-piece trace selector, let $M$ be the labels whose every elementary proper pc-minor is dismantlable ample. No affine subspace $L\subseteq\mathbb F_2^6$ satisfies $X_t\in\mathsf{Damp}$ exactly when $t\in L$ for all $t\in M$; in particular no single partition-equality condition works on this domain. Instead, for $t\in M$, positivity is exactly $(t_0=t_1)\lor(t_2=t_3)\lor(t_4=t_5)\lor(t_1=t_3)$.
proof: The positive labels $010000$, $111010$, $110000$, $000000$, and $111111$ all lie in $M$ by explicit orders and minor closure. Any affine classifier containing $000000$ is linear and, if it contains the other four, must also contain their sum $100101$, which is the original forbidden labeling and also lies in $M$. This contradiction proves nonaffinity. Every negative member of $M$ is pc-minimal by definition and minor closure, so negating the exact four-inequality forbidden selector yields the displayed four-equality disjunction.
